items.title: Sayaji Hotels enters Himachal Pradesh with the launch of Enrise by Sayaji in Kufri
items.snippet: Sayaji Hotels has announced the launch of Enrise by Sayaji, Kufri, marking its entry into Himachal Pradesh and expanding its presence to 10 states across India. Developed in association with KC Vilaas, the 64-room property is located in Fagu, Theog, near Shimla, catering to leisure and business travellers.

items.title: Silvāna Hotels and Resorts Enters Raipur with 81-Room Property
items.snippet: Silvāna Hotels and Resorts has entered the Raipur hospitality market with the launch of its first 81-room hotel on Airport Road, positioning the property around experiential stays, nature-inspired architecture and destination-led hospitality. The property has been designed around an existing garden on the site, with the architectural concept incorporating natural materials, earthy tones and flowering trees.

items.title: Karjat-Bhimashankar ropeway plan awaits government approval
items.snippet: A proposed ropeway connecting Karjat in Raigad district to the Bhimashankar temple could make pilgrimage journeys easier for devotees travelling from Mumbai and nearby regions. The estimated ₹650-crore project aims to provide an alternative to road travel. Former state minister Dilip Walse Patil outlined the proposal during his visit to Bhimashankar to review ongoing temple development works.

items.title: Nagaland CM seeks month-long PAP relaxation for Hornbill Festival
items.snippet: Nagaland Chief Minister Dr Neiphiu Rio has urged the Union Home Ministry to extend the Protected Area Permit (PAP) relaxation during the Hornbill Festival 2026 from 10 days to one month. He has also sought a year-round exemption for foreign tourists visiting the state.

items.title: Airlines warn of diplomatic fallout over slot cuts
items.snippet: Four airlines have written separately to MIAL and the ministry of civil aviation (MoCA), escalating the dispute to diplomatic channels, said sources. The carriers have sought MoCA intervention and warned of escalation to the govt, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and aviation authorities in their respective countries, including possible reciprocal measures under bilateral agreements.

items.title: ITDC Reports 12.6% Profit Growth in Q2 FY27
items.snippet: India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC), a Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, reported a 12.6 per cent year-on-year increase in Profit After Tax (PAT) for the second quarter of FY 2026–27. The growth was attributed to improved operational performance, efficiency measures and continued business development across its tourism and hospitality portfolio.

items.title: US Revokes Over 6,000 Visas Linked to Birth Tourism
items.snippet: The US Department of State has revoked more than 6,000 visas from foreign nationals found to have engaged in or facilitated birth tourism, the department announced on November 12. The announcement comes as the Trump administration intensifies its crackdown on the practice and the commercial networks allegedly operating around it.

items.title: US ground stop lifted as airlines restart flights
items.snippet: The US ground stop ended, allowing airlines to restart departures after communications problems disrupted air traffic control. However, the resumption of flights did not immediately restore airline schedules. The Federal Aviation Administration said the nationwide restriction followed communications issues affecting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

items.title: Scotch whisky import dispute likely to be resolved 'very soon': Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal
items.snippet: The government is hopeful of resolving the ongoing Scotch whisky import shipment issue within the next few days, with the Department of Revenue working to address concerns related to product classification, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Friday.

items.title: Municipal Corporation of Delhi draws up stricter inspection norms for eateries, may issue sealing notices
items.snippet: In a bid to elevate food safety standards, the MCD has launched stricter inspection protocols for eateries across the city. Inspections will assess hygiene practices, the quality of water used, and the sources of food supplies. Establishments that do not conform to these standards could face penalties or even closure.
